articles.body:
Peacock is a streaming platform owned by NBCUniversal, which is a subsidiary of the larger Comcast Corporation. The streaming service first launched back in April 15, 2020 for Xfinity customers only before launching nationwide on July 15, 2020. According to the most recent Q2 earnings call in July 2026, Peacock is currently sitting at about 48 million paid subscribers.

IGN's streaming service coverage is managed by Blythe Dujardin . Additional contributions are made by:

Peacock currently offers three different subscription tiers with monthly an annual pricing. There is also a couple of streaming bundle options with Walmart+ or Apple TV. Peacock raised the price of its service in August 2026 , which is now reflected below:

The best streaming bundle for Peacock is the Apple TV bundle that launched in October of last year. This gets you both services for a discount, but you'll only get no ads on both if you opt for the Premium Plus bundle option. Outside of that you can choose to get a subscription to Walmart+, which includes access to either Peacock Premium or a Paramount+ plan. You'll have the choice to switch between the two every 90 days. Walmart+ is currently the only way to get a free trial of Peacock in 2026.

The Peacock Select plan will only get you access to TV shows from NBC, Bravo, and a few other networks owned by NBCUniversal. If you want to get the full Peacock library, you'll need to upgrade to one of the Premium plans available. This gets you access to movies and Peacock Originals.

Some of the most notable offerings on Peacock are popular sitcoms like The Office, Parks and Rec, and Law and Order. It's also the only place you'll be able to watch originals like Paper or the latest season of Traitors. Outside of TV shows, Peacock also gets access to movies from Universal Pictures and Focus features. This includes popular franchises like the Jurassic World movies , Shrek , and all of the Kung Fu Panda movies . The service also tends to get first dibs on any Illumination films like The Super Mario Galaxy movie .

Peacock also offers a variety of live sports streaming , including things like NFL football and the Olympics.

articles.title: Death Stranding movie nabs director of Pig and A Quiet Place: Day One
articles.summary: The live-action adaptation of Hideo Kojima’s Death Stranding video game taps Michael Sarnoski as its director
articles.body: The Death Stranding movie, an adaptation of Hideo Kojima’s supernatural UPS delivery guy walking simulator, has its director. A24 has announced that Michael Sarnoski will both direct and write the project. Sarnoski’s previous work includes directing the surprisingly stunning Nicolas Cage drama Pig and monster movie thriller A Quiet Place: Day One. Death Stranding, released in 2019, tells the story of Sam Porter Bridges (voiced and performed by Norman Reedus), a porter tasked with ferrying packages across a devastated United States. Along the way he is assaulted by oily-looking monsters called BTs, rain that makes you old, and more conventional enemies including a terrorist sect led by a man named Higgs who is played by Troy Baker. The game went on to critical success, winning several Game Awards and netting Kojima an award for best direction. A sequel, Death Stranding 2: On the Beach has been announced and launches June 26th. The Death Stranding movie was announced in 2023. Kojima, an ardent lover of cinema, announced the feature-length production would be headed by A24 with a shirt featuring dripping letters similar to the logo for Death Stranding. A24, an independent production company, is known for championing quirky, weird, and downright disturbing films like Hereditary, Everything Everywhere, All at Once, and the forthcoming Death of a Unicorn. Death Stranding, with its surrealist visuals and storytelling, feels like a good fit for Sarnoski.

articles.title: How to Get Reptile Leather - Enshrouded Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Reptile Leather is a crafting material in Enshrouded, which can be used to make a Medium Backpack upgrade and various armor at the Blacksmith, Alchemist, and
articles.body:
Reptile Leather is a crafting material in Enshrouded , which can be used to make a Medium Backpack upgrade and various armor at the Blacksmith, Alchemist, and Hunter. The type of leather you're after will determine which creatures you'll want to seek out, so here's a straightforward guide that tells you exactly what to look for.

Reptile Leather is "a sturdy material used in extravagant tailoring" and can either be picked up as dropped loot or crafted on the Drying Rack. To get the Drying Rack, you'll need to complete the early quest Hunter Becomes the Hunted and have the Hunter in your base. The Drying Rack is one of the Hunter's production places, and to craft it, you'll need 10x Wood and 6x String .

You'll then need to obtain Reptile Hide to be able to craft Reptile Leather. The recipe for making Reptile Leather is: 1x Reptile Hide and 3x Salt . This will give you 3x Reptile Leather.

To get Reptile Hide, you'll need to visit the Blackmire in the northwest of Embervale and look for Snapjaws. Specifically, the easiest place to guarantee you find them is the Snapjaw Tar Pits.

Water Reptile Leather is a higher-level version of Reptile Leather and is described as a "shiny material with an interesting texture." Water Reptile Leather has almost the same recipe as Reptile Leather, but instead, you'll need 1x Water Reptile Hide and 3x Salt . Again, this makes 3x Water Reptile Leather.

The good news is you can get Water Reptile Hide early on in your exploration of the Veilwater Basin. If you enter the area from the Albaneve Summits and go through the Passage to Veilwater Basin, you'll arrive at Veilwater Basin Outlook.

Northwest of here is Dragondream Lake , where you'll find Driftwood Wake, Tavern "Ol' Salt 'N Pepper", and Ol' Captain's Rest. On the northwest edge of Dragondream Lake is where I had the best luck finding a group of amphibians that I could get Water Reptile Hide from.

articles.title: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra review: show off
articles.summary: The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra features a unique Privacy Display to keep wandering eyes off your screen. It’s a useful update to a feature-packed phone.
articles.body: “Someone might be watching everything I’m doing on my screen,” I tell myself in public. Even when I’m doing nothing of consequence — just making my little Wordle guesses — there’s a sense of unease that stays with me. It’s never bothered me too much, and I generally save the sensitive stuff like banking for when I’m home, but I realize it’s a feeling I’ve internalized whenever I’m on my phone in a crowded place. Using Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra for the past couple of weeks has offered some relief from that particular worry simmering in the back of my mind; it solves a problem I didn’t even fully recognize until I started using it in my daily life. I used the S26 Ultra in a lot of places where people could have been looking over my shoulder. Planes, airports, crowded convention halls… wherever I was, the phone’s new Privacy Display really did relieve that feeling of discomfort. It’s not totally bulletproof — I’m sure someone could have made out my Wordle guesses if they were trying pretty hard to look at the dimmed screen — but just the knowledge that a casual glance wouldn’t reveal the way I’d missed the obvious solution four guesses in a row was enough. And the fact that I can turn it off when I’m back at home? That rules. The question is, how much is that peace of mind worth? And how confident can you be in the display’s ability to keep prying eyes away from real stuff like passwords, not just puzzle games? Those are the $1,300 questions. [Product: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra | I tend to think of the S26 Ultra as existing in a class by itself. Can you think of another phone with four rear cameras? A built-in stylus? Performance specs up the wazoo? It attracts a particular kind of fan. So I think your interest in the S26 Ultra as a whole package should be your guiding star if you’re interested in the Privacy Display but unsure about the rest. It is a phone person’s phone — big, expensive, wonderful — with one especially cool new feature we haven’t seen anywhere else. I can even see a world where this display tech is slowly adopted by other phone makers until it’s something we take for granted. That’s a feature worthy of the Ultra’s lofty title. Elsewhere, the S26 Ultra is more familiar. It offers a versatile camera, an all-day battery, and Samsung’s mixed bag of Galaxy AI features. This time, Samsung implemented a couple of smart AI tools that seem to borrow from Google’s Pixel phones, which aren’t tremendously useful now but are generally heading in the right direction. Now Nudge, modeled on Magic Cue, offers contextual suggestions based on what’s being said in a text conversation. I’m miserable at adding things to my calendar, and I find this extra bit of help genuinely useful. Now Nudge seems to work only in some narrowly defined use cases within the messaging app, and I only saw it pop up a couple of times. Still, on one occasion it helped me check my calendar and schedule an event. [Image: Just as I was preparing to publish this review, another AI feature appeared on the S26 Ultra by way of a software update: Gemini task automation. It’s limited to ordering food and rideshare apps right now, but the idea is that you give Gemini a simple prompt, like “Get me an Uber to the airport,” it opens the app in a virtual window, and it goes about using the app to fulfill your request. In some quick preliminary tests this has worked as advertised so far; crucially, Gemini stops before the final step so you can review and submit your order yourself. This, I think, is a good idea and certainly makes me feel better about using it. There are all kinds of ways to feel about this concept of computers using computers, and I have much more testing to do, but if it works consistently then this seems like a pretty significant step toward AI assistants that can actually do useful things for us. Over in the gallery app, things are a little weirder. Samsung has built in some generative AI capabilities designed to help you reimagine your photos in fun ways, but for me they were unsettling. The company seems intent on zipping right past “Photos are memories” and into “Photos are whatever the hell you want them to be.” With the S26 series, you can tell the phone how you want to edit the photo with natural language prompts, like you can in Google Photos. You can change your outfit, add makeup to your face, and generally mess with your photos until they no longer even resemble anything that actually happened. It’s bananas. Thankfully there are some basic guardrails in place. I couldn’t get Samsung’s AI to completely remove my clothes or dress me in a bikini. It did oblige when I asked it to remove my husband’s shirt in a photo — it even extended the tattoos visible on his arm further up toward his shoulder. It will happily let you download a photo of a celebrity from the internet, paste them into your own selfie, and make it look like you happened upon Adam Driver while you were at the park and he posed for a picture with you. And then it can come up with some real weird stuff: I asked it to add my husband to a picture of me and it put him in my lap like a little ventriloquist dummy. This stuff is weird, I don’t like it very much, and I can’t shake the feeling that it gets harder to trust what we see in a photo every time companies like Samsung and Google add generative AI tools like this. As for the camera itself, there’s more good news for fans of hardware updates: Two of the S26 Ultra’s cameras come with brighter apertures. The main 200-megapixel camera now uses an f/1.4 lens compared to f/1.7, and the 5x telephoto is now f/2.9 versus f/3.4. Wider apertures mean these cameras can, in theory, create more detailed images in low light since they’re able to use lower ISOs or faster shutter speeds as needed. And that bears out in my side-by-side testing. The main camera consistently uses a lower ISO than the S25 Ultra, while they both stick to a shutter speed of 1/120 second. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: I see the same behavior on the 5x compared to the S25 Ultra in moderate lighting. In very dim light, both phones raise ISO to 1250, but the S26 Ultra is able to use a faster 1/60th shutter speed compared to 1/30th on the S25. Longer exposures will result in more noise that the camera has to smooth out in post-processing, and you’ve got a better chance of getting a sharp image with a faster shutter speed while shooting with the telephoto camera. These are real, unequivocal improvements to the camera system, and I will take them every day over a thousand bland generative AI photo editing features. Underneath all that, the S26 Ultra is still an object you can hold, and it’s a nice one — if a little big for my taste. It loses what was left of its Note heritage by trading the boxy corners and sharp edges for the softer curves used by the S26 and S26 Plus. The seam along the sides of the screen where glass meets frame (aluminum this year, we’re all done doing titanium I guess) is smoother than on the S25 Ultra. The S Pen silo is also right on the corner, so the end of the stylus is curved slightly on one side — now there’s definitely a right way and a wrong way to fit it into the frame. [Image: [Image: The dimensions are similar to last year’s, but the S26 Ultra looks and feels much sleeker; the silver S25 Ultra looks like the Cybertruck of phones next to it. One similarity I’m disappointed to see carrying over to this year is the lack of Qi2 magnets, which are handy for thwacking the phone onto a magnetic charger or using MagSafe PopSockets and the like. Samsung is still outsourcing those to its cases, which is bad news for those of us who don’t put cases on our phones. Otherwise, the display remains huge at 6.9 inches, and although the phone feels a bit more comfortable to hold than last year’s model, this is still a very big phone. But the Privacy Display is the big story here. The screen uses a technology Samsung calls Flex Magic Pixel to limit the viewing angle when Privacy Display is engaged. So the question is: Does it look any different with Privacy Display turned off? Next to the S25 Ultra, they look basically the same head-on, but I can see more of a color shift from the S26 Ultra when I view it from a very low angle. This never really bothered me while using the phone, but some people are more sensitive to that kind of thing. [Image: [Image: When you turn Privacy Display on, the screen dims slightly and the picture looks a bit flatter. Again, this might be a problem for some people, but it didn’t really bug me; after a few moments I didn’t really notice. You can enable Privacy Display just for notification banners, which is awesome, and it’s kind of wild to see the effect working on just that part of the screen. Notifications look a little dim and gray, like the ghost of a notification. I left Privacy Display on for days, only remembering once I tried showing someone next to me something on my phone screen (which they had to squint at to make out). At its default setting, Privacy Display makes it harder to see what’s on your screen from an angle — but not impossible. Especially if there’s white text on a black background, someone standing next to you is still going to be able to read it. [Image: [Image: [Image: Enabling the option for “maximum” privacy protection makes it much harder to make out text on the screen from an angle, though it also lowers contrast more dramatically when you’re looking at it straight on. It would be handy if you could keep Privacy Display engaged at its default setting for general use and then kick it into maximum privacy for certain apps; given all the ways Samsung lets you customize these kinds of features, it wouldn’t surprise me if Samsung is working on that for version two. For the past couple of years, the Ultra seemed to be losing parts of its identity without picking up any meaningful improvements along the way. Sure, the switch from a 10x to a 5x zoom was probably the right one in the long run. And I can’t say I’ve missed any of the Bluetooth features that used to come with the S Pen. But altogether, it just seemed Samsung wasn’t quite sure what to do with this big phone — and a name like “Ultra” sets the standard pretty high. [Image: A big phone with some new ideas. Things are different this year. This phone genuinely does things I haven’t seen another phone do, and that’s not a phrase I’ve been able to apply in a long time. Privacy Display works, it doesn’t come with any serious downsides, and it’s eminently useful. Even my usually tech-disinterested husband was impressed. The camera upgrades are real, too: Faster lenses let in more light and offer you a better chance of taking sharp photos. It’s not some AI nonsense, it’s just physics. The S26 Ultra is a return to form in some ways, but it remains a pricey device and generally A Lot of Phone. But that’s kind of the Ultra promise: unapologetically big, crammed with every feature you can imagine. This is still a phone for a self-selecting group of people, but I’m happy to report that fans of the series are finally getting an update that’s worthy of the name. Photography by Allison Johnson / The Verge --- Agree to Continue: Samsung Galaxy S26, S26 Plus, and S26 Ultra Every smart device now requires you to agree to a series of terms and conditions before you can use it — contracts that no one actually reads. It’s impossible for us to read and analyze every single one of these agreements. But we started counting exactly how many times you have to hit “agree” to use devices when we review them since these are agreements most people don’t read and definitely can’t negotiate. To use the Galaxy S26, S26 Plus, or S26 Ultra, you must agree to: * Google Terms of Service * Google Play Terms of Service * Google Privacy Policy (included in ToS) * Install apps and updates: “You agree this device may also automatically download and install updates and apps from Google, your carrier, and your device’s manufacturer, possibly using cellular data.” * Samsung End User License Agreement * Samsung Privacy Policy * Samsung Terms and Conditions There’s also a variety of optional agreements, including: * Provide anonymous location data for Google’s services * “Allow apps and services to scan for Wi-Fi networks and nearby devices at any time, even when Wi-Fi or Bluetooth is off.” * Send usage and diagnostic data to Google * Google Gemini Apps Privacy Notice if you opt in to using Gemini Assistant * Send diagnostic data to Samsung * Samsung personalized advertising * Bixby personal data intelligence Other features, like Google Wallet, may require additional agreements. Final tally: seven mandatory agreements and more than seven optional agreements.

articles.title: The Hollow Event Guide, Puzzle Walkthroughs, and UGC Items - Core Roblox Guide - IGN

articles.body:
The Hollow is a server-wide Roblox event that runs from October 23 to October 31 , with a live finale scheduled for Halloween. It's a celebration of the many popular horror game experiences on Roblox, including Animal Hospital, 99 Nights in the Forest, Dandy's World, Piggy, and more. Each day brings a new challenge, with puzzles to solve, mazes to escape, and monsters to avoid. In this complete guide to The Hollow event on Roblox, you'll find detailed walkthroughs on how to complete each daily quest and the unique UGC rewards you'll get for doing so.

Daily Floor Guides and Game Walkthroughs

Each day, a new floor of the movie theatre maze becomes available. There will also be a special event to participate in for a popular horror game.

Each day, an entity from nine games will stalk the movie theatre maze. Outside the theatre, you will also find portals that will take you to each game , so you can complete the game-related quest and unlock a unique reward.

Little Shop of Terror UGC and Avatar Items

Inside the movie theatre, you can visit the concessions stand to spend your tickets on the following items.

Shines a bright line into the darkness and scares certain entities away

Spots nearby entities, turning your screen black and green

A device that detects when an entity is nearby

Allows you to be invisible and sneak past an entity without getting caught

There are additional games that you can play during The Hollow, which will either earn you tokens or UGC Rewards.

You'll find teleports outside of the movie theatre to the following games with UGC Rewards.

At the concessions stand, you can choose to teleport and visit games. Each day, there will be featured games that will net you double tickets.

To participate in The Hollow, head directly to the official page of The Hollow .

Each day, you'll see a new monster featured. The event runs for nine days from October 23 to October 31, but you can continue to earn rewards until November 2.

The first event begins on October 23, starting at 11 AM PT. You can subscribe to any of the available events to get the Roblox Present's Little Plus-tergeist companion.

articles.title: All Sha-Chi Amber Fragment Locations - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Throughout your time in Phantom Blade Zero, you'll come across Sha-Chi Fragments, which are required to increase your Sha-Chi meter. These fragments
articles.body:
Throughout your time in Phantom Blade Zero, you'll come across Sha-Chi Fragments, which are required to increase your Sha-Chi meter. These fragments won't be enough on their own, though, as you'll need four of them to form a full Sha-Chi Amber to see your Sha-Chi increase. Luckily, we have a full breakdown of all of the Sha-Chi Amber Fragment locations by area in Phantom Blade Zero.

All Sha-Chi Amber Fragment Locations in PBZ

If you're looking for a specific area, just click on the map below to go directly to it.

Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Amber Fragments

Throughout the Weeping Creek Valley in Phantom Blade Zero, you'll find four different Sha-Chi Amber Fragments. Collecting all four will give you one full Amber Fragment, which can be used to upgrade one of your abilities at any of the nearby Bells.

You may not be able to hit every Sha-Chi Amber immediately, as some require collecting a Phantom Edge before being able to progress or open a new area. Below you'll find the locations of all four Amber Fragments.

Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Amber Fragment 1

On the main path south of the Broken Puppet Valley Bell. You'll discover a headless enemy with a shield. Defeat the group of enemies here, including the headless knight and you'll find the Sha-Chi Amber Fragment in the purple glowing chest.

Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Amber Fragment 2

You'll obtain this Amber Fragment after defeating a group of enemies northeast of the Rustblade Pavillion Bell. Luckily, this one is on the main story path, so you won't miss it.

Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Amber Fragment 3

Just north of the Outpost Bell you'll see a wall that can be broken using the Dread Axe Phantom Edge. Destroy the wall and clear out the enemies in the newly open section. Upon killing the last enemy you'll automatically get the next Sha-Chi Amber Fragment

Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Amber Fragments 4

From the Long Pillar Overlook Bell, go across the wooden bridge. From here, follow the path on the right-hand side. This will include wall running over a small gap. Keep going straight until you see a small metal door in the rock face. Use the Rusted Long Key (which you'll obtain in a gold chest next to the Crane Bell at the Long Pillar Overlook) on the door on the side of the mountain. Inside, there are a few enemies; dispatch all of them to get the final Sha-Chi Amber Fragment found in this section

articles.title: Not So Scary After All - Enshrouded Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Not So Scary After All is a side quest in Enshrouded that’ll send you to Pikemead’s Reach in search of a friendly little plushy doll. The Barber
articles.body:
Not So Scary After All is a side quest in Enshrouded that’ll send you to Pikemead’s Reach in search of a friendly little plushy doll. The Barber is certain that’ll it’ll help the Farmer overcome her fear of fell critters, so he sends you into harm’s way to procure one. This side quest walkthrough will show you where to find it with minimal mortal danger.

For tips on how to have the best experience in Enshrouded, check out the following pages:

You can start Not So Scary After All after unlocking the Bard and giving him proper shelter. Once he’s had time to get cozy in your settlement, he’ll meet the Farmer and learn of her fear of fell critters. Then, he’ll send you on this quest.

To complete Not So Scary After All, you need to head into Pikemead’s Reach and find a basement under one of its homes. The fastest way to get to Pikemead’s Reach is to glide west from the Nomad Highlands Ancient Spire. You can run along a few cliffs on the way to keep your elevation until the final descent to the south gate of the ruined city.

Approach from the Huckster’s Square entrance on the south side of Pikemead’s Reach. Then, turn right down the first alleyway you see inside the Shrouded mist.

Turn left at the end of the alley and head up the stairs ahead of you. You’ll reach a grate at the far end. Climb up it and look to your left.

The ruined house you’ll find there near the Shroud vase is the one with the basement you’re looking for. Head down the stairs inside and through the passages you find there.

In the room at the end of the underground passage, you’ll find the plushy resting in the rubble . Pick it up and bring it to the Farmer to finish this quest, earning you 100 XP and a cute little plushy you can place in your home for some added Comfort.

articles.body:
The distance between getting the Hunter's Chain Sickle and the Iron Gauntlets is pretty drastic, so don't be alarmed when you haven't picked up a new Phantom Edge just yet. The Iron Gauntlets pack a strong punch with a base damage of 261 and base Guard Break of 223. They have incredibly high Shield-Breaking power that rivals the Dread Axe.

They do not have a use outside of combat.

How to get the Iron Gauntlets in Phantom Blade 0

You'll get the Iron Gauntlets in Phantom Blade 0 by defeating Stone Hand Iron Fever in the Crimson Forest. This is part of the main story questline, so you won't miss out on getting the Iron Gauntlets if you progress naturally through the zone. Upon defeating the Stone Hand Iron Fever, the Iron Gauntlets will be automatically given to you.

The Iron Gauntlets ability reads as follows: Press R2 repeatedly to perform up to 3 fist attacks. A full combo consumes 1 Remnant Spark.

articles.title: Kevin Feige, Marvel Studios, and Hugh Jackman Pay Tribute to Sir Patrick Stewart After Actor's Death at 86
articles.summary: Kevin Feige, president of Marvel Studios and COO of Marvel, has given a heartfelt response to the death of acclaimed actor Sir Patrick Stewart.
articles.body:
Kevin Feige, president of Marvel Studios and COO of Marvel, has given a heartfelt response to the death of acclaimed actor Sir Patrick Stewart.

Stewart, best known for his roles as Jean Luc Picard in Star Trek and Charles Xavier in Marvel’s X-Men films, died on Wednesday, October 28 following a brief battle with Alzheimer's and Lewy Body Dementia. His family broke the news in a public statement on October 29.

As shared by Variety, Kevin Feige gave a touching eulogy to the celebrated actor and knight following the news of his death.

“I’ll never forget the first time I saw Sir Patrick Stewart on the set of the first X-Men,” Feige said. “After years of knowing him as the inimitable Captain Picard, I was in awe — and he turned out to be everything I had seen on screen and more: brilliant, charming, warm, generous, with a quiet strength and gravitas.”

“Away from the cameras, he was even more remarkable, with a wonderfully sharp sense of humor. It was a true privilege to know him and to work with him. His legacy lives on not only in decades of extraordinary work, but in the many, many people he mentored. He will be deeply missed.”

Marvel Studios also released a statement after in a post on its official Twitter/X account.

“All of us at Marvel Studios are deeply saddened by the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart. Sir Patrick brought Professor Charles Xavier to life with extraordinary grace, intelligence, and humanity, defining the character for generations of fans, from X-Men to Logan to Avengers: Doomsday. He was a singular talent, a generous collaborator, and a true gentleman. Our hearts go out to his wife Sunny, his children, his friends, and the countless fans around the world whose lives he touched with his art.”

Hugh Jackman, who starred alongside Stewart as Wolverine, also shared a tribute to the actor on Instagram, along with two photos from their time working together.

"We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days," he wrote.

On Twitter/X, James Mangold, the director of Logan, posted a wordless tribute to Stewart. His post included a GIF from Logan and a photo of an empty wheelchair. Heartbreakingly, it's worth noting that the film followed an 'old man Logan' as he cared for a sickly and aging Charles Xavier who also suffered from dementia.

David Hayter, who wrote the 2000's X-Men movie, also shared a post remembering Stewart. "Damn. He was so kind to me on the X-MEN set. I was so touched to see his magical friendship with Ian McKellen bloom on that film. A true gentleman. A wellspring of effortless charisma. A galaxy-spanning talent. Thank you for the memories, Professor," he wrote.

On Instagram, fellow Star Trek and X-Men actor Rebecca Romjin recalled her time on set with Stewart in a short video, fondly remembering him as "positively delicious, hilarious, and naughty," with an "incredible sense of humor and a booming voice that always spoke to the back of the room, as every clasically-trained Shakespearean great needs to master."

The Russo Brothers, who famously directed some of the biggest and most iconic films in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, spoke out about their time working with Stewart in a public statement .

"We’ve been lucky enough to work with some of our childhood heroes. And Sir Patrick Stewart will always be one of them. A legendary actor with an unmistakeable presence, and an unmatched integrity. Thank you for entertaining all of us, sir. And for teaching us humanity, both on and off the screen. Sending our love to your family, friends, and fans around the world," they said.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart's Best Roles in Movies and TV
articles.summary: Patrick Stewart's best roles in movies and TV went far beyond outer space and mutants.
articles.body:
2026 has taken a great many beloved celebrities from us. We thought nothing could rival the pain of losing Dolly Parton , but now comes the news that Patrick Stewart has passed away. Stewart, of course, rose to prominence as the lead of Star Trek: The Next Generation in the ‘80s and ‘90s, before going on to headline Fox’s X-Men movies. But even those two venerable franchises are just a taste of Stewart’s brilliant and prolific acting career.

As we come to terms with this profound loss, let’s take a look back at Stewart’s most memorable roles over the years, covering some of cinema’s most iconic heroes and a few dastardly villains for good measure.

Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men Series (2000-2026)

Casting Patrick Stewart as Professor Charles Xavier had to have been one of the easiest layups in Hollywood history. He’s a famously bald man with a penchant for mentoring up-and-coming heroes with rousing monologues. That’s not to say that Stewart didn’t continuously bring his A-game to the various X-Men movies, especially whenever he shared the screen with Ian McKellen’s Magneto.

We particularly cherish his late-career turn in 2017’s Logan, where he displayed a new level of frailty and regret. And as much as we’ll miss the actor, it’s comforting to know we’ll get one last opportunity to see him play the role in Avengers: Doomsday.

The I, Claudius miniseries might have been the most stacked ensemble cast in TV history. It really says something that Stewart stands out so well among that group – Derek Jacobi, Siân Phillips, Brian Blessed, John Hurt! – despite his relatively young age. Yes, it’s more than a little surreal seeing him with a full head of hair, but Stewart truly owns the role of Roman soldier Sejanus.

We’re so used to seeing Stewart play morally upright heroes like Captain Picard and Professor X that it’s always something of a shock to see him cast as a villain instead. Stewart was cast very much against type as a Neo-Nazi skinhead ringleader in this 2015 action-thriller from director Jeremy Saulnier, and that’s what makes the role stand out. Stewart is chilling here, bringing a calm but palpable sense of danger to every scene.

Before Josh Brolin brought master swordsman Gurney Halleck to life on the big screen, there was Stewart’s version. He may be best remembered for sauntering across the desert battlefield while holding a pug, but Stewart delivered a memorable performance all the same in this campier take on the Frank Herbert novel. You can immediately understand why the warriors of House Atreides would follow their captain into battle without question.

Stewart showed us a very Ahab-like side of Captain Picard in 1996’s Star Trek: First Contact, so it’s only fitting that he would go on to actually play the obsessive sea captain in a TV movie version of Moby Dick. As you’d expect, Stewart is phenomenal in the role, earning both Golden Globe and Emmy nominations for his performance.

Deputy Director Avery Bullock in American Dad (2005-present)

American Dad is definitely another case of Stewart being cast against type, and once again, that’s precisely why the role works so well. Stewart’s innate charisma and soothing voice clash mightily with the ridiculous situations the series frequently thrusts him into. Bullock is a real highlight of this long-running animated sitcom, and one of the reasons American Dad has come to eclipse Family Guy in popularity.

Scrooge, Tiny Tim and the Rest in A Christmas Carol (circa 1991)

OK, this isn't from a movie or show, but... When not in space or training mutants in Westchester or doing some other crazy sci-fi stuff, Stewart was often on stage. It’s where he came from, of course, as a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company, and as Star Trek: The Next Generation began to wind down, he found himself back doing theater often. One of his most memorable turns on stage was in his one-man-show version of Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, where he played some 40 characters himself! Who could forget the moment where he wept for Tiny Tim? We wept too!

Before Star Trek, before X-Men, Stewart was one of King Arthur’s knights! In fact, he was King Arthur’s father-in-law, specifically in John Boorman’s Excalibur. This was a Stewart who was still getting his sea legs in movies, and his role in the film isn’t huge – but it is memorable. “It’s the boy king!” he hollers in that way only Sir Patrick Stewart could, as young Arthur rides to the rescue early in the movie. Looking back on the film now, his presence is powerful.

Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek (1987-2023)

And then there’s Jean-Luc Picard, a character who we all love today but who wasn’t necessarily welcomed with open arms back when The Next Generation debuted in 1987. Fans are gonna fan, and frankly, first-season Picard did take a bit of getting used to, as even Stewart himself would later admit that he had to acclimate to a life of shooting episodic, American television and being around a kind of wacky cast of co-stars in Jonathan Frakes, Brent Spiner, et al.

But the funny thing about that is, it’s pretty clear that those crazy Americans helped to complete Mr. Royal Shakespeare Company in a way that might never have happened if he hadn’t put on the spacesuit. As Stewart grew into the role of Picard, a humanity emerged that became the bedrock not just of TNG, but really of Star Trek for an entire, well, generation. Make it so, Sir Patrick. Make it so.

What are your favorite Patrick Stewart roles? Let’s discuss in the comments!

articles.title: How to Use the Evaporator - Probably Stolen Guide - IGN

articles.body:
The Evaporator is an item you can get when you begin Probably Stolen as a Chemist. You can also unlock it when you purchase the Chemistry set, giving you access to a variety of useful tools. These can be tricky to master, especially while you're trying to run a business. In this guide, we'll be sharing with you how to use the Evaporator and best utilize it as you play Probably Stolen.

How the Evaporator Works in Probably Stolen

At its core, the Evaporator is a tool that assists in cleaning up water or any type of liquid you place into the input section. You can optionally use it in the two steps that you get in the base Chemistry 101 Guide, and in the third step for Dream Dust and the Caffeine Pill.

Following the second step of getting the chemical to the temperature range you need it to be, bring it over to the Evaporator. You'll need to stick it onto the Container portion of the object, and let it sit there. The Evaporator only works at night, and you won't be able to see the result until the next day.

After you've used it, the amount in the Container portion should be significantly less, highlighting that the water or alcohol is gone. You can then move on to the next step, allowing you to proceed to use the Chem Finisher and wrap up your recipe. The real trick is making sure to let it sit overnight and seeing it the next day.

You'll know it's worked correctly when there's a fraction of what you previously had when you put the container into your Evaporator the night before.

Chocolate Cheers is the first in a Quest series that unlocks a new Hello Kitty Island Adventure mini-game . To begin it, you must unlock Pompompurin's Dessert Boat via completing the Quest Revive the Oasis , and reach Friendship Level 15 with Pompompurin by giving him his favorite Gifts.

Talk to Chococat, who is usually found near the Crafting Table beside the Resort Gate Fast Travel Mailbox . He tells you that he is investigating if chocolate ice cream is still delicious, and requests your help.

Head to Pompompurin's Dessert Boat in Gemstone Mountain and make two Chocolate Ice Creams using the following materials:

Cactus Cream x 2 - picked from cacti in Gemstone Mountain

Chocolate Coin x 2 - found in and around the Shipwreck in Rainbow Reef

After giving Chococat his chocolate ice cream, he notes something curious: Pompompurin is not there! He finds a note that says Pompompurin is out exploring, which worries Chococat because Pompompurin is usually quite lazy.

Leave the Dessert Boat and talk to Chococat just outside. He figures that Pompompurin is napping, and asks you to find him.

Pompompurin turns out to be to the left of the corral where the Rockadoodler Round-up mini-game is played , near the starting point of the Corral Stampede challenge course . Talk to him to try to learn what happened, but he falls asleep before he can tell you!

Only one thing can wake Pompompurin: his favorite Mama's Pudding . Make one Mama's Pudding at the Dessert Boat using the following ingredients:

Cactus Cream x 1 - picked from cacti in Gemstone Mountain

Coral Milk x 1 - found in crates or growing from plants in Rainbow Reef

When you gift the Mama's Pudding to Pompompurin, he wakes up enough to tell you that he found a "sweet rock" in the Crystal Caves, but has not been able to find it again. He drifts off to sleep yet again.

Talk to Chococat inside the Dessert Boat. He is curious about the sweet rock and decides to investigate more, telling you to check back again tomorrow!

Peacock has a solid lineup of movies and original TV shows for November, kicking off with the addition of major franchise favorites like Fast & Furious and Spy Kids. But the most notable new releases for the streamer are some promising Peacock Originals and the streaming debut of Andrew Garfield's The Uprising.

First up, there's a six-episode thriller miniseries called The Good Daughter, which adapts the popular 2017 novel of the same name. Then, later this month, we're getting a new comedy series called Dig from the mind of Amy Poehler.

If you're wondering what's worth watching, we've gathered together some of our top picks right here. You can also jump to all of the new releases for November for the full list by day.

Technically the third movie in the Fast and Furious franchise (though not chronologically), Tokyo Drift took the series in a totally different direction. This was the first Fast movie directed by Justin Lin and focuses on teenage street racers in Japan. It was the least popular film in the franchise in terms of box office numbers, but it's definitely worth a rewatch.

The Uprising, which was briefly marketed as a Robin Hood origin story , is the latest Andrew Garfield film. Taking place in 14th century England, the movie follows a lowly farmer as he escalates toward the Peasants' Revolt of 1381. With a solid cast of characters, it's worth a watch if you didn't catch it in theaters. As a Peacock exclusive, this is the first time it will be available on a streaming service.

Created by Michael Shur and Amy Poehler, the show follows four archeologists working at an excavation when they discover a surprising secret that drops them in the middle of an international conspiracy. articles.title: James Gunn Says It 'Won't Be Too Long' Before DCU Batman Is Cast, Will Be Close in Age to David Corenswet's Superman
articles.summary: James Gunn has revealed that DC Studios is finally getting ready to cast the DCU's Batman.
articles.body:
James Gunn has revealed that DC Studios is finally getting ready to cast the DCU's Batman.

Speaking on a new podcast about James Gunn's Suicide Squad film, the director and DC Studios boss addressed where he's at when it comes to the next Batman. Although Robert Pattinson is playing the current caped crusader, it's expected that he will exist in his own separate universe , away from James Gunn's DCU, while another Batman will join forces with the likes of Superman.

He noted that it "won't be too long" before they begin casting the next Batman and debunked rumors that he's already been cast. He noted that he's open to casting anyone for the role, even if they've been in a previous DC movie like The Suicide Squad.

"When we do cast the DCU Batman, which isn't very far away, if I gave someone a day role in Suicide Squad that is going to be the best Batman, then I am not going to rule him out from that. I want to get everyone into account. One of the things that excites me about casting is being able to pick a Batman that is actually the best actor for that role. Supermans have always been chosen on who the best actor for that role is. And for some reason, Batmans are always chosen as movie stars."

Gunn also noted that he is taking age into account for the role, and stated that whoever they go with will likely be around the same age as David Corenswet, who plays Superman. He noted that the two characters are pals and contemporaries, which means they can't be too far apart in age. As a result, you can likely expect the next Batman to be in their low to mid-30s, which has historically been the sweet spot for the role, minus Ben Affleck, who was playing an older version of the character.

As of right now, it remains to be seen who will get the job. Batman is a beloved character and one that a lot of actors would love to take a crack at. Gunn also recently noted that Batman is one of the three main characters for DC's future , as one would expect. Some were hoping the role would go to Alan Ritchson, but the actor confirmed he's been having conversations with the studio about a non-Batman role, and DC Studios boss Peter Safran recently revealed they're trying to find a good character for him to play. As Gunn noted though, it could be someone we're not as familiar with. That worked out wonderfully with David Corenswet, who plays a great version of the Man of Steel. If casting is expected to begin soon, we may know who the next Batman is next year.

articles.summary: In the Quest Chocolate Cheers, Pompompurin revealed that he found a "sweet rock" inside the Crystal Caves of Gemstone Mountain. One day later, you
articles.body:
In the Quest Chocolate Cheers , Pompompurin revealed that he found a "sweet rock" inside the Crystal Caves of Gemstone Mountain. One day later, you can begin the next Hello Kitty Island Adventure Quest , Great Mines Think Alike, and work with Chococat and Pompompurin to find the sweet rock again!

Talk to Chococat, who is thrilled to be investigating a new mystery. He suggests that you meet up with Pompompurin at his Dessert Boat in Gemstone Mountain, so head there.

Enter the Dessert Boat and talk to Pompompurin inside. He tells you that he is extremely motivated to find the sweet rock again, and is going to climb Gemstone Mountain to do so!

Meet Pompompurin at the closest entrance to the mines, north of the Oasis lake. When you talk to him there, he says that he can't remember exactly where he found the sweet rock, but there was a red crystal nearby.

Enter the Crystal Caves through the entrance behind Pompompurin. You will find yourself in a room filled with pink crystals - not the color you are looking for!

Walk straight along the wooden slatted path in front of you until you reach a glowing red door.

Go through it to find yourself in a room filled with red crystals. Keep walking straight, keeping the river on your left. About halfway through the room is a single red crystal on the ground with a blue exclamation point over it.

Interact with the crystal. There's no sweet rock, but Pompompurin remembers something else: water balloons in a green cave.

Continue walking straight through the red crystal room, keeping the river on your left. You will reach a glowing orange door - walk through it.

This room has orange crystals, so it's not the one you need. Continue following the wooden slatted path, which moves through the center of the room. You will cross two rivers as you go.

You will end up in the top right corner of the orange room, where you will find a glowing green door. Go through this door.

In the room with green crystals, the path splits into two. Follow the north pathway along the upper edge of the lake. Just past a glowing white door that leads outside, there are water balloons on the ground with a blue exclamation point over them.

Interact with the water balloons. The sweet rock isn't there, and Pompompurin doesn't get any memories back this time.

Head outside through the glowing white door. Pompompurin and Chococat are just outside. Talk to Pompompurin, who is disappointed. Then, talk to Chococat, who points out that a tunnel collapsed nearby and it has caused some strange objects to appear!

There are three pieces of Rock Candy on the ground to your left. Pick up all three, and then talk to Pompompurin. He confirms that these are the sweet rocks he found before, and he wants more!

Chococat says that it is possible to re-open the blocked tunnel entrance, but it will require a lot of work. Return to the Dessert Boat and talk to Chococat there. He brainstorms a list of materials you need for his plan.

Meet Chococat at the Crafting Table in Gemstone Mountain, located west of the Gemstone Town Fast Travel Mailbox and north of the large cluster of Visitor Cabins. Talk to him again to learn exactly what you need to collect:

Banana Ice Cream x 3 - made at the Dessert Boat using a total of 3 Cactus Creams and 3 Bananas

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Adds 'Non MilSim Content' Disclaimer to Halloween Themed Content
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added new disclaimers to content that may not abide by the game's usual grounded tone and aesthetic.
articles.body:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added new disclaimers to content that may not abide by the game's usual grounded tone and aesthetic.

Earlier today, Modern Warfare 4 added a new mode known as Possession. It's a Halloween-themed mode that lets players "possess" the person they last killed, allowing you to both teleport to their last location and take their loadout. It's a really interesting idea for a mode, but of course, it doesn't adhere to the game's grounded, gritty, and more realistic tone. So, Infinity Ward added a "non-milsim content" disclaimer tag to the playlist before players search for a match.

The new Possession MP mode added to Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 includes a warning: "Warning: Non-MilSim Content" The new mode is a Halloween themed MP mode — CharlieIntel (@charlieINTEL) October 29, 2026

The new Possession MP mode added to Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 includes a warning: "Warning: Non-MilSim Content" The new mode is a Halloween themed MP mode

This comes after years of players getting frustrated that Call of Duty's multiplayer often abandons the darker, more serious tone established by the campaign and seasonal lore drops. The franchise has added skins that allow players to play as Nicki Minaj, Beavis and Butthead, and Seth Rogen, which has come at the cost of the game's identity. Infinity Ward already promised to dial things back with Modern Warfare 4 and not include absurd, over-the-top skins, but this new disclaimer does suggest there will be some content that may ride a line for hardcore fans.

Of course, you can also make the argument that Call of Duty isn't realistic and it isn't really a "milsim" game, since it's so fast-paced and filled with ridiculous movement, Wolverine-style health regeneration, and more. It's more of an aesthetic than a style of play. Still, some players value the immersion of more realistic military characters and modes and don't want that disrupted.

It's unclear what Infinity Ward's plans are for bundles in the future, but the team recently outlined its plans for Modern Warfare 4 Season 1, and a lot of it seems to retain the grounded tone that fans desire. Of course, we'll have to wait and see what's in store in the new year, which is often when we start to see more crossover content.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Brewers-Rays Game 5 clincher ends World Series on viewership high note
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers’ World Series clincher on Wednesday made this year’s Fall Classic relatively on par with other World Series this decade in viewership,...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers' World Series clincher on Wednesday made this year's Fall Classic relatively on par with other World Series this decade in viewership, with the usual boost from Nielsen's recent methodology updates.

The Brewers' title-clinching Game 5 win over the Tampa Bay Rays averaged 14.22 million viewers across Fox and Fox Deportes, according to preliminary figures the network released. If the figure holds, Game 5 would be functionally even with last year's Dodgers-Blue Jays Game 5, which averaged 14.30 million viewers, and would surpass all Game 5 audiences between 2019 and 2023.

When including the preliminary figure from Game 5, the full five-game series averaged 11.83 million viewers across Fox, Fox Deportes, and Univision, which would put the series' viewership level with Astros-Phillies in 2022 (11.76 million viewers) and Braves-Astros in 2021 (11.74 million viewers), both of which had six games. Viewership will predictably fall short of Dodgers-Yankees in 2024 (15.10 million viewers) and Dodgers-Blue Jays last year (15.49 million viewers), but will easily surpass Rangers-Diamondbacks in 2023 (9.08 million viewers), the least-watched World Series of all time.

Of course, given Nielsen's recent methodological changes, this year's World Series was likely less watched than both 2021 and 2022, despite being level with those years on paper. Since then, Nielsen has expanded its out-of-home viewing measurements to cover 100% of the country and also began incorporating its Big Data sample into the top-line viewership figure. Both changes have generally increased viewership for live sports compared to prior years, particularly for major live events like the World Series. However, both the 2021 and 2022 World Series went six games and benefited from higher viewership in Game 6, lifting the overall average.

It's safe to say the Brewers-Rays outperformed expectations, especially since the series went only five games. Before the series, many feared two smaller-market teams with no clear superstars might replicate 2023 viewership levels. That proved not to be the case, with all but one game eclipsing 10 million viewers.

articles.title: This WNBA Finals stat is good omen for Valkyries in Game 7 against Dream
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries came into Game 6 looking to close out the WNBA Finals and secure the franchise’s first championship, but they were blitzed by the...
articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries came into Game 6 looking to close out the WNBA Finals and secure the franchise's first championship, but they were blitzed by the Atlanta Dream , 80-69, and thus, will have to play in a winner takes all Game 7 on Saturday . However, the Valkyries might have a little history on their side.

Coming into this series, there have been 13 times in WNBA history where the Finals have come down to a deciding game. The team with homecourt advantage has won 11 of those Finals series, as per Alexa Philippou of ESPN. This will be the 14th WNBA Finals to come down to a winner takes all game, and that stat certainly bodes well for the Valkyries against the Dream.

Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals will be held at Chase Center, the home arena of the Valkyries. During the playoffs this season, they are 6-1 on their home court with their sole loss coming to the Dream in Game 2 of this Finals series.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

This is also going to be the second time in the last three seasons that the WNBA Finals has come down to the final game of the series, as per Philippou. Although the league only switched to a best-of-seven format last year, in 2024, the New York Liberty defeated the Minnesota Lynx, 3-2, when it was still a best-of-five series.

No matter who wins the series on Saturday, it will be the first title in franchise history for both teams. The Valkyries are only in their second year of existence as an expansion team, while the Dream have reached the WNBA Finals in 2010, 2011 and 2013 but were unable to cross the finish line.

articles.title: Stranded Walkthrough - Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: After taking shelter from the storm during Survivors, our Modern Warfare 4 campaign guide picks up with Stranded, the game's tenth mission. Compared to
articles.body:
After taking shelter from the storm during Survivors , our Modern Warfare 4 campaign guide picks up with Stranded, the game's tenth mission. Compared to previous missions, this is an open-ended sandbox area with dozens of collectibles to find if you're looking to fully complete MW4 and get all of the achievements/ trophies.

This walkthrough section will be just for the main three objectives to progress the story, so be sure to check out our more in-depth guides for collecting every note, yellow crate, and shipping container code in Stranded if you're wanting to find everything:

There are three main objectives in order to finish Stranded, and they can be done at any time by either making your way there manually or fast traveling. You can do them in any order, but here's a good route to follow. Click the text to be brought to the specific section:

After finishing the first of three objectives, Tap to Reveal .

Prioritizing the SAM site first will unlock a handful of supply drops around the map that'll help purchase upgrades at Base Camp, so it might be best to tackle this one first.

Once you gain control of Park at Base Camp, grab the parachute and Sang 9mm handgun off the table, and turn around to chat with Sgt. Jae about the current situation. Once you’re finished, climb the stairs and open the hatch to exit.

Meet Kal at the edge of the building, and he’ll give you the option of fast traveling straight to the objective or breaking off to find supplies. Once you’re ready, make your way to the SAM site by either heading there the long way or fast traveling.

If you fast travel to the SAM Site, you'll spawn across the river. Cross it, taking out the guards on the docks to enter the main SAM site island.

Once it's clear, Kal and Dunn join you, then a vehicle patrol rolls by - go prone or take cover to avoid it. Continue through the snow approaching another bronze monument, then head right to use another house as cover.

Your allies start opening fire, so make your forward and take out any enemy in your path. Turn around to find a massive collection of explosives and ammo for the next section.

You don’t have a lot of time to prepare before truckloads of enemies show up, but do your best to scatter proximity mines and C4 around the immediate area. If you have any bomb drones leftover, you might be able to take out entire squads before they even arrive if you time them right.

At the base of the statue there are even more explosives to kit yourself out with, and an open yellow crate that contains Night Vision Goggles that does not count towards opening every yellow crate for the Time to Crate achievement . To the left of the statue is a yellow crate for this achievement, and right above is the SAM Site Note About Helipad note.

Hold them off until an armored BMP arrives, which you’ll need to take out using explosives. Luckily there’s plenty of thermite at the cache at the base of the statue, so get as close as you can without getting blasted and lob thermite at the vehicle. Two to three should be enough

Kill the Remaining Enemies at the SAM Site

Take out any stragglers that may have survived your initial defense. Using thermal here to spot them is another useful tactic.

Meet up with Kal and Dunn to Detonate the Explosives

Join up with Kal and Dunn behind the lumber to detonate the explosives around the SAM turrets. Once you’re done, you can fast travel back with Kal or continue exploring. Now that skies are clear, three supply drops land around the map for you to loot.

On arrival, you’ll see three enemies immediately ahead. If you’re jumping into this mission from the beginning with just a pistol, it’s recommended to head left up the ladder to take out the enemies on the roof to grab better weapons to take on the rest of the outpost’s occupants. Once the area is clear, feel free to scour the surrounding buildings for more weapons, ammo, and supplies, which you can use to repair items back at Base Camp.

Once you’re ready, follow Kal to the bunker entrance where you’ll find supplies one of the many yellow supply crates scattered about the map. Open the hatch and head down.

Once you open the hatch, you have to complete this section before you can leave and continue exploring.

Slide down the ladder, and follow Kal to the submarine bay until you breachable a door. Head to the right to find the Provisions note, then head left to proceed. Follow Kal down the stairs and into the water.

When you resurface on the other side, you’ll find a pair of locked double doors and hatch that should open after hitting the red button on the right, but the power is out.

Follow Kal down the grate he pulls up and dive into the water.

Climb back up through the opening after swimming through to take out two enemies. Your new objective is to find and repair the power generator. It’s in the middle of the room, but not accessible. Let's plug in the wire first.

Submerge yourself at the back of the room, then follow the yellow wire to the source of the problem - it’s been unplugged, and the area is gated off like the generator room.

Dive back in via the grate you came back up in, but swim to the left to find the opening. Climb up and reconnect the wire.

Submerge yourself again in at the same point you did when plugging the wire back in, at the back of the room, and turn around to head back towards the generator. If you’re getting low on breath, find grates in the floor above you to refill your air.

The opening to the generator area is slightly to the left of where you entered while submerged; climb the opening to find the silenced Rezi 12 shotgun and start the generator.

The locked double doors are now open, and a trio of enemies are here to die. Take them out, then head back towards the red button and press it now that the power is back on.

Go through the door and hook a right to find some supplies, then go back towards the main submarine depot room.

Keep following Kal into an office-like room, and grab the note Discipline off of the desk. There’s also some supplies on a shelf. Head right and continue to the munitions depot.

Grab the ammo, supplies, and throwing knives from the center console, then jump down through the shattered windows in front of you into the water below. The explosives are in crates marked with a yellow triangle .

Enemies spawn as you start to explore. You can take them out quietly by surprising them out of the water, or traditionally by blasting their faces off.

Either way you’ll find a yellow triangle-marked crate on the opposite end of the room from where you entered that you’ll have to climb, which triggers more enemies to spawn. Turn around and go back in the water and head left to, then climb the stacks to find another explosives crate. If you turn to your right while still on this platform, you’ll find another crate within jumping distance. Jump over and grab the bombs. Just be careful about the enemies.

Take out the rest of the enemies, then Ko directs you to the north door. Wait for Kal to breach the door, watch him baptise an enemy, and continue straight through. Swim through the linear path and come out a stairwell with two goons waiting for you and take them out. Head toward the stairs grabbing the two supplies, then open the door to find even more supplies; ammo, frag grenades, flashbangs, and another shotgun. Don’t forget to grab the note Traitors from the desk on the left.

When you’re ready, breach the door with Kal, taking out the three enemies he flashbangs. Head left towards the ladder that brought you down here to finish this objective.

Once you’re ready, head to the Jamming Station. Upon arrival to the mission marker, follow the stairs to the right up the hill. Climb the small cliff using the wooden planks, grab the supplies to your right, and keep moving.

Keep scaling the mountain; this is a linear path until you reach a dead soldier. Pick up the heartbeat sensor (it's very useful in just a bit), as well as supplies and the note Cliffside Dead Soldier Note . Turn around and keep taking the stairs up the mountain. You’ll get shot at by two enemies as you climb, but Kal takes one out, leaving the other for you.

A bridge collapses as you try to cross it, but you can time your jump to the other side well enough to not have to backtrack.

Keep going, but watch out for the recently-spawned helicopter’s spotlight - time your movement to not get caught. You can use boulders for cover to wait for the helo to move by, then keep booking it.

Fight Through the Plateau to Reach the Jamming Tower

Once you reach the summit, use your trusty new heartbeat sensor to track enemies that are hard to see in the snowstorm. Take out the first guard you see quietly (you might still have a few throwing knives in your backpack), then plot your course through to the jamming tower - avoiding the main road. If you get caught, an alarm will sound and a bomb drone starts hunting you until it loses you.

Enter the building on the right to quietly take a few enemies out, and if you entered through the bottom floors doors you can find the Jamming Station Quarters Note immediately to your left on a counter.

Once you’re clear to enter the main jamming station area, head into the door at the north side of the compound to immediately find the Jamming Station Main Room Note on a bench. The next room has a few enemies who attack, with one above you you should watch out for. There’s a yellow push cart in the center of the room, and you can move it over to a previously unattainable window to the left to find a Mojave .357 magnum to use.

Head outside towards the tower and climb the ladder, where you’ll find another yellow crate with Scout Drone inside. Start scaling the tower by climbing up a copper pipe. A bomb drone comes whirring into view, but Kal takes care of it from afar.

Find the red and white caution taped ledge and continue climbing. As you reach the top, Kal takes out an enemy who’s spotted you. Climb and turn right to take out another, the bomb drone operator.

It’s on the ground where you killed the drone operator.

Head back outside to find green chests that contain the bomb drones and pick some up. Use R1 to whip one out and fly one or two into the enemies that have spawned on the ground. Keep climbing the tower by vaulting over destroyed stairs, and reach the top with the electrical panel.

Open the Jamming Equipment at the Top of the Tower

A helicopter zeroes in right as you open the jamming equipment panel.

Use the Bomb Drones to Destroy the Helicopter

Two hits from bomb drones is enough to take out the helicopter, but make sure you take adequate cover to operate them as it’ll still wail on you with shots.

Parachute off the Collapsing Jamming Tower

Once you take out the helicopter, it crashes into the tower, sending you plummeting to your death unless you deploy your parachute. Landing safely completes this objective.

When you’re ready, head back to Base Camp to find that Cho has succumbed to his wounds. Interact with his body to say your final goodbyes to your fallen comrade. Talk to the Kal to continue the story.

The game keeps a separate save for Stranded if you want to come back later to finish anything other collectibles you've missed, so don't feel pressured to stick around if you want to continue the story.

When Ready, go to Base Camp to Leave for the FOB With Your Allies

Clear up any loose ends in this snowy wasteland, then talk to Kal at Base Camp to leave for the airbase and end the mission.

articles.title: Romance Guide - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Romance is now possible in Crimson Desert with the release of the Charting the Unknown DLC, and each playable character can marry almost any of the NPCs in
articles.body:
Romance is now possible in Crimson Desert with the release of the Charting the Unknown DLC, and each playable character can marry almost any of the NPCs in Pywel. This is an expansion of the existing NPC Trust mechanic from the base game, and the new interaction UI will help you deepen your bonds. This guide will show you how to flirt with, romance, and marry NPCs in Crimson Desert's Charting the Unknown DLC.

To romance a character in Crimson Desert, you have to repeatedly flirt with them to build their romance meter up to 100. Once you've flirted enough, you can propose and they'll hopefully accept. Romance is entirely separate from the base game Trust system, so you'll have to start from scratch even if you already have 100 Trust with your favorite NPC.

Nearly all of Pywel's NPCs can be romanced barring a few exceptions. Certain NPCs (like Pywel's Witches ) require you to complete specific quests before they can be romanced as well. If an NPC can be romanced, you'll see a Trust meter with a heart in the top-right corner when interacting with them.

If you cannot romance an NPC, there will be a crossed out person with a heart next to the Interact prompt when targeting them. Most of the Greymanes seem to be off limits to Kliff, for example.

Choosing to flirt with an NPC will raise their romance level by a few points. You can speed up the romance process even further by chatting about past adventures or giving gifts as well. You can only increase an NPC's romance level with these methods once per in-game day .

Once you've reached the maximum romance level of 100 with an NPC, you can successfully propose to them. Don't try to propose before reaching 100 romantic Trust points! Otherwise, they'll reject your advances and lose 15 Trust points.

After getting married, your spouse will permanently be marked on the map like the other playable characters. You can also summon and travel together with your spouse, and they'll periodically give you small gifts. When you're not adventuring with them, they'll hang out at your primary residence at the Greymane camp or any new residences constructed in the Charting the Unknown DLC.

You can also change your spouse's appearance at a barber shop, but don't expect full character customization. It's similar to the customization available to Kliff, Damiane, and Oongka. Finally, you can divorce your spouse from the revamped interaction menu if you get tired of them.

This page is still being updated as we discover new details about romance in Pywel. In the meantime, check out these pages for more Crimson Desert tips:
